exercises.title: Reuse 1 — which dimension of reuse?
exercises.problemHtml:
Wiegers Table 18-1 describes any reuse situation along three dimensions: the extent of reuse (how much material: one requirement, with its attributes, or with associated artefacts), the extent of modification (unchanged, attributes changed, or the requirement tweaked) and the reuse mechanism (copy vs reference). Which dimension does each statement describe?

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Ba chiều của tái sử dụng: mức độ tái dùng, mức độ sửa đổi, cơ chế (sao chép vs tham chiếu).

Yêu cầu

  • Trả lời mọi câu trong khung trả lời rồi bấm Nộp.
  • Đúng hết mới được Accepted; giải thích từng câu hiện sau khi nộp.

exercises.title: Reuse 2 — copy or reference?
exercises.problemHtml:
Copy-and-paste is the crudest reuse: no history of origin, the copies can be edited independently, and copying within a project bloats the specification. Reuse by reference is usually better: collect reusable items in a shared location, give each a unique id, and insert the id (and a link) in your document. The master must be accessible and persistent.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: Reuse 3 — benefits of reuse
exercises.problemHtml:
Benefits of reusing requirements: faster delivery, lower cost, consistency within and across applications, higher productivity, fewer defects and less rework; trusted requirements save review and test time and improve estimation; users see consistent functionality.

exercises.title: Reuse 4 — what can be reused?
